explanations: In `groupsWithRetry`, an abort makes `fetchGroups` reject with an AbortError, which is not a DirectoryError, so it is treated as retryable: the loop sleeps (100, 200, 400 ms) and calls the directory again with the already-aborted signal, repeating until all attempts are used. Cancelled or timed-out requests keep the handler alive and burning attempts for up to ~700ms after the deadline instead of stopping immediately. The loop should check `signal.aborted` (rethrow) in the catch and make the sleep abortable.

Non-retryable DirectoryErrors are rethrown immediately; the signal is not aborted, so the handler's catch takes the 502 branch. 504 is only sent when the signal is aborted, and nothing turns the error into an empty list.

The `close` event fires after the response is fully written as well as on disconnect; checking `writableEnded` restricts aborts to genuine early disconnects. Responses are guarded separately, the timer is cleared in finally, and keep-alive is unaffected.

The same `ctrl.signal` is passed to `rolesForGroups`, so the deadline abort rejects it; the catch sees `ctrl.signal.aborted` and sends 504. The deadline covers the whole handler, not just the directory call, and partial results are never returned.
